constraints.text: Do not explain or interpret what the reader can already infer from action or dialogue; trust the scene.
Avoid overly symmetrical, polished, or mechanically balanced prose patterns; allow natural variation in sentence shape and scene emphasis.
Avoid narrator signposting such as speculative 'sanki/belki' commentary when concrete action can carry the meaning.
Do not make every recurring object, image, or detail symbolic or meaningful; remove decorative motifs that do not affect character, action, or atmosphere.
Dialogue does not need to teach, validate, summarize, or advance the plot on every line; allow brief, specific, characterful reactions.
Do not force a neat moral, emotional summary, generic smile, or tidy thematic echo at the ending; finish on a concrete character-specific beat.
Prefer observable behavior over narrator labels for emotion, intention, evaluation, or subtle mental state.
After a strong image, joke, action, or line of dialogue, do not add a sentence explaining why it matters.
